weather_report:
West Perth dozes under a charcoal sky, the air cool and faintly metallic, as if the night has been rinsed clean. Cloud hangs thick enough to halo the streetlights and soften the edges of buildings, and toward dawn light rain is expected to slip in and settle through the early morning. Sunshine will be scarce at first, perhaps only a muted shimmer if the cloud thins; UV is low at this hour and will stay gentle through breakfast, then lift if breaks appear later. The day looks grey-leaning and softly blurred rather than stark, with damp roads and the hush that comes with drizzle.

It’s a light-shell and closed-shoes kind of morning, an umbrella in the bag and layers you can peel if the air warms. Start slowly: brew something warm, glance at the sky between songs, and let the rain decide your pace. After sunup, errands go best between showers, a tram ride is more pleasant than a drive, and a seat by a window at a quiet cafe may be the day’s small luxury. If the cloud loosens later, a short walk will feel new-washed; if not, keep the hood up and the shoulders loose, and remember a touch of sunscreen by late morning just in case.
